name: Agriculture and Food Security
summary: Calorie sources and land use, field practice and crop diversity, controlled-environment agriculture, fisheries under the Thalassar Accord, livestock and welfare grading, fermentation, nutrient loops, reserves, and food security outcomes.

calorieSources.name: Field agriculture
calorieSources.summary: Grains, pulses, oil crops, and tree crops, where field production is genuinely superior.

calorieSources.name: Controlled-environment agriculture
calorieSources.summary: 1.1 million facilities producing nearly all leafy vegetables, berries, fruiting vegetables, and out-of-season produce on 1/400th of the land field agriculture uses.

calorieSources.name: Marine capture and aquaculture
calorieSources.summary: 210 Mt annually under the Thalassar Accord framework.

calorieSources.name: Fermentation and cultured protein
calorieSources.summary: Precision fermentation and cultured tissue; the fastest-growing category for two centuries.

calorieSources.name: Livestock on pasture and rangeland
calorieSources.summary: Down from 34% of calories before the founding, by economics rather than prohibition.

landUseNote: Livestock shares the 26.4 M km^2 of managed forestry and rangeland recorded in planet.biosphere and is not counted again here.

cropDiversity.rationale: Nobody can sell a seed bank held by a purpose-bound trust.

controlledEnvironment.note: Growing food outdoors at 68 degrees north in Auroria is possible and pointless.

governingFramework.name: The Thalassar Accord framework
governingFramework.summary: Modern Concord fisheries law descends directly from the first binding planetary treaty, agreed on fisheries only in 14 BE by people who could not agree on anything else.

principalFisheries.name: Mistral Shelf fishery
principalFisheries.summary: Richest fishery on Elysium, built on Silverdrift shoals.

principalFisheries.name: Amarant Upwelling fishery
principalFisheries.summary: Second largest; productivity falls sharply in warm Amarant phases, so quota is set on multi-year averages.

fisheries.overExploitedNote: Both in Elandric coastal waters, both under mandatory recovery plans, and both the subject of an unresolved dispute between the Region and the Commission about whether assessment or enforcement failed.

declineCauses: cultured and fermented protein became cheaper
welfare law made husbandry more expensive

domesticates.name: Durn
domesticates.summary: Large grazing Zoaea kept for meat and milk.

domesticates.name: Pell
domesticates.summary: Smaller flock animal kept for fibre and meat.

welfare.rationale: A civilization that intends to be wealthy without cruelty cannot exempt the part of its economy where cruelty is cheapest.
welfare.derogationCritique: The Concord's own welfare panel describes the pastoral derogations as inconsistent with the regime's stated basis.

fermentation.culturalNote: This food is ordinary. It is not marketed as a substitute for anything, most living Elysians have never eaten anything else in that category, and the historical debate about whether it counts as real food is studied in schools as a curiosity.

reserves.financialRejectionRationale: A claim on food is not food, and the circumstances that would require the reserve are exactly the circumstances in which claims fail.

tiers.name: Concord strategic reserve
tiers.summary: Grain, pulses, oils, and fermentation feedstock in 340 dispersed depots.

tiers.name: Regional reserves
tiers.summary: Regional staples held to regional specification.

reserves.sizingScenario: Three consecutive warm phases of the Amarant Oscillation causing delayed or failed Elandric monsoons in successive years, coinciding with a Sirocc drought.

foodAsRight.foundersReasoning: A right to food would be a right to a physical thing the state cannot guarantee in all circumstances, and a right that fails in a famine is worse than no right at all.
foodAsRight.canonPosition: An open constitutional question, not a settled design.

affordability.canonNote: No Elysian goes hungry because food is unavailable; some do because they are unwell.

hazardResponse.name: Elandric monsoon failure
hazardResponse.summary: Regional reserve draw and interregional transfer; no planetary action required.

hazardResponse.name: Sirocc drought
hazardResponse.summary: Aquifer ceilings, desalination transfer, and Alcyon flow-share reallocation.

hazardResponse.name: Amarant warm phase
hazardResponse.summary: Fishery quota reduction set years ahead on the 14-month forecast.

hazardResponse.name: Compound scenario
hazardResponse.summary: Never observed; met by the Concord strategic reserve with emergency powers available.

flowShare.principle: Allocation by turn, published in advance, with the shortfall shared rather than concentrated.
flowShare.note: Modified beyond recognition in its mechanics and unchanged in its principle. Constitutional lawyers cite it more than any other precedent; farmers simply use it.

forecastLead.canonNote: This capability, not the reserve itself, is what most distinguishes the modern Concord from the civilization that lost 210 million people to a supply failure it did not see coming.

knownWeaknesses.name: Nutrient leakage
knownWeaknesses.summary: 8% loop escape and seasonal hypoxia in four Regions, with no agreed solution and an active political fight.

knownWeaknesses.name: Two over-exploited stocks
knownWeaknesses.summary: Under recovery plans, with Region and Commission disputing whether assessment or enforcement failed.

knownWeaknesses.name: Cultivar concentration despite the rule
knownWeaknesses.summary: The 15% cap applies per species; three staples are dominated by closely related cultivars satisfying the letter and not the purpose.

knownWeaknesses.name: CEA energy dependence
knownWeaknesses.summary: 24% of calories depend on 0.31 TW; an extended grid failure is a food failure, and the 14-day islanding rule is what stands between them.

knownWeaknesses.name: Pastoral derogations
knownWeaknesses.summary: Cultural exemptions from welfare law that the Concord's own welfare panel calls inconsistent with the regime's stated basis.

knownWeaknesses.name: Amarant vulnerability
knownWeaknesses.summary: The second-largest fishery loses productivity in every warm phase, roughly one year in seven, and no management change alters that.

knownWeaknesses.name: Food is not a Charter right
knownWeaknesses.summary: Three amendment attempts, the last narrow; an open constitutional question.

knownWeaknesses.name: Food insecurity is not zero
knownWeaknesses.summary: 2.9 million people, concentrated among the severely unwell; a health failure appearing as a food statistic.

knownWeaknesses.name: Reserve cost is invisible until needed
knownWeaknesses.summary: 0.6% of GCP annually against a scenario never observed; canon notes such holdings historically erode when a generation passes without using them.

knownWeaknesses.name: Bottom-decile food share
knownWeaknesses.summary: 16.4% against a 9.1% median; food is cheap for most and not for everyone.

knownWeaknesses.name: Compound scenario untested
knownWeaknesses.summary: The reserve is sized against a combination that has never happened, so the sizing rests on modelling rather than experience.

knownWeaknesses.name: Regional reserve specification drift
knownWeaknesses.summary: Three Regions hold stocks poorly matched to a planetary distribution effort.
